bull_bear.body:
- Three decades of execution experience across multiple infrastructure asset classes, with more than 100 projects completed since 1995
- Established, long-standing relationships with government agencies including NHAI, MPIDC, PWD, IDA and MPRRDA
- Proprietary toll management platform developed in-house for real-time revenue monitoring, discrepancy detection, leakage control and site-level management, giving stronger operational control and a more efficient cost structure
- Among the select toll operators to have implemented ANPR-based toll collection, with toll plazas operated on major inter-state and intra-state expressways
- Asset-light OMT toll model: short contract tenure recycles working capital quickly and carries no long-term exposure to asset degradation or major rehabilitation costs
- Capital discipline: a stated gross profit floor of 13-14% in bidding rather than pursuing low-quality volume
- Government entities account for 64.9% of the EPC order book, offering execution certainty and payment security
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Government policy and budgetary dependence — The forward-looking statement explicitly names changes in government policy and economic conditions as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. The demand narrative in this bundle rests almost entirely on public spending - Union Budget capital outlay, MoRTH and NHAI allocations, NIP, PM Gati Shakti and the National Monetisation Pipeline - so a slowdown in state capex or a change in tolling/highway policy directly compresses both order inflow and toll opportunity.
- Project execution risk — Project execution is named in the forward-looking statement as a risk factor. The Company's stated long-term positioning - 'the future will be shaped by execution, contract by contract' - and its record order book mean value is realised only on delivery; slippage on active contracts converts a record book into deferred revenue.
- Competitive intensity in bidding — Competition is listed as a risk factor in the forward-looking statement, and growth is explicitly framed as depending on 'selective, margin disciplined bidding'. Aggressive bidding by peers either costs the Company work or forces it below its stated margin thresholds.
- Segment and revenue concentration — Tollway Collection accounted for 73.7% of FY26 consolidated revenue, with EPC Infrastructure 19.8% and Real Estate and Others 6.5%. Management's own rationale for geographic expansion is that it 'is intended to diversify revenue concentration', which acknowledges that current revenue is concentrated by both segment and geography (a central India base).
- Growth dependent on entry into unproven adjacencies — A stated pillar of growth is measured entry into wayside amenities, renewable energy EPC, ropeways and HAM projects under Parvatmala Pariyojana, plus MLFF tolling - all described as opportunities under evaluation rather than businesses with an operating track record, so the growth case carries execution and learning-curve risk in segments new to the Company.
- Balance sheet leverage as the Company scales — The Company treats leverage as an active watch item: debt to equity was reduced from 0.9x to 0.45x over FY23-FY26 and management 'remains focused on balance sheet quality, leverage discipline, and returns' as it scales - implying that funding a fivefold order book without re-levering is a live constraint.
- Environmental and clearance compliance at construction sites — Environmental priorities are stated as responsible material usage, dust and noise management at construction sites, and compliance with clearance conditions - a structural exposure for a civil-construction contractor, where a clearance breach can halt a site.
- Safety framework still being formalised — Site-level safety protocols, trained safety personnel and mandatory incident reporting are in place, but the report states that 'further formalization through digital tracking and third party audits remains a stated priority' as the Company grows - i.e. safety assurance has not yet caught up with the scale of operations.

business.body: HIL operates and manages toll collection systems on highway stretches won through competitive bidding, principally under short-tenure Operate-Maintain-Transfer contracts with NHAI or the relevant government authority, where it pays a fixed weekly/daily sum irrespective of actual collections. It also executes EPC civil works spanning roads, bridges, irrigation works, tanks and civil buildings for public and private clients, including projects under PMAY, PMGSY and the Jal Jeevan Mission, and develops and sells residential and commercial property while earning lease rental income from hospitality and commercial assets. Tollway collection is the largest revenue driver, followed by EPC Infrastructure, with real estate the smallest vertical; activity is anchored in Madhya Pradesh with expanding presence in Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Chhattisgarh.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Four-pillar growth strategy: growth through scale and adjacency, operational excellence, geographic expansion, and disciplined balance sheet management.
- Scale the core verticals through selective, margin-disciplined bidding, holding a stated gross profit discipline of 13-14% and a willingness to exit non-viable contracts rather than chase low-quality volume.
- Expand from the central India base into Gujarat, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and the Northeast, with a longer-term aim of broadening presence further across India to diversify revenue concentration and deepen access to new order flows.
- Measured entry into adjacencies aligned with existing mobility-infrastructure credentials: wayside amenities and ancillary services alongside toll corridors (food courts, fuel stations, EV charging, warehousing, driver facilities), renewable energy including solar EPC and EV charging infrastructure, and potential participation in ropeways and HAM projects under Parvatmala Pariyojana.
- Prioritise traffic-intensive corridors to maximise toll collection revenue, and undertake larger EPC projects either independently or through joint ventures.
- Leverage the proprietary in-house toll monitoring and site-management technology (including ANPR experience) as the operating edge in Tollway Collection and to create synergies across infrastructure segments.
- Monetise real estate faster through residential delivery plus commercial and hospitality leasing for recurring income.
- Maintain balance sheet quality, leverage discipline and returns as the Company scales; debt to equity was reduced from 0.9x to 0.45x over FY23-FY26 and net worth increased to Rs 228.5 crore.
- Long-term intent to build a larger, more diversified mobility infrastructure platform with broader geographic presence and stronger recurring income streams.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: HIL's expansion in this bundle is described as footprint and adjacency build-out rather than plant capex. Geographically, the Company is expanding from its central India base into Gujarat, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and the Northeast, with a longer-term target to broaden its presence further across India in order to diversify revenue concentration and deepen access to new order flows. Growth through scale and adjacency is a stated pillar, with four adjacencies under evaluation: commercial leasing and real estate monetisation through hospitality and commercial properties; ancillary services alongside toll corridors including food courts, fuel stations, EV charging, warehousing and driver facilities; potential participation in ropeways and HAM projects under Parvatmala Pariyojana; and renewable energy opportunities including solar EPC and EV charging infrastructure. The Company has already commissioned EV charging infrastructure under the AICTSL contract in Indore and is evaluating renewable energy EPC as a growth area. Over the medium term, MLFF tolling, the wayside amenities programme and ropeway development under Parvatmala Pariyojana are identified as meaningful adjacency opportunities, while in EPC the project pipeline in Madhya Pradesh and expanding opportunities in Gujarat and Goa support continued growth. Funding capacity was strengthened during FY26: the Company listed on the BSE and NSE on 12 August 2025 and raised Rs 130 crore through the IPO, which the report says strengthened the capital base to support future expansion and strategic initiatives; net worth rose to Rs 228.5 crore and debt to equity improved from 0.9x to 0.45x over FY23-FY26. No rupee capital-expenditure quantum, project cost, commissioning date or capacity addition is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Government infrastructure-led development remains the primary demand driver, with infrastructure capital outlay projected to reach Rs 13.1 lakh crore by FY27, roughly 14% above FY26, and continued support from the National Infrastructure Pipeline, PM Gati Shakti and the National Monetisation Pipeline.
- Higher allocation to road and highway development, continued expressway execution and rising toll collections create a favourable backdrop for both of HIL's main operating segments.
- Toll collection demand is underpinned by an expanding national highway network, PPP participation, economic and trade growth lifting freight traffic, urbanisation, and electronic tolling technology (ETC, RFID, real-time traffic management) that improves collection efficiency.
- Near-universal FASTag penetration improves toll realisation and minimises revenue leakage, supporting predictable and transparent cash flows for toll operators.
- The Indore and wider Madhya Pradesh operating environment is supportive: the Indore Municipal Corporation's sanctioned budget focused on road construction, upgradation, maintenance and restoration works gives regionally established EPC contractors execution visibility.
- Under the OMT model, fixed weekly/daily payments to NHAI are independent of actual toll collected, so revenue upside above the bid assumption accrues to the operator while short tenure allows faster capital turnover and limits long-term asset risk.
- Better enforcement, lane discipline and FASTag penetration are the stated margin levers in toll operations; in EPC, margin is protected by the 13-14% gross profit bidding floor.
- Mix shift: Tollway Collection contributed 73.7% of FY26 consolidated revenue, EPC Infrastructure 19.8% and Real Estate & Others 6.5%, with Real Estate revenue stepping up from Rs 8.0 crore in FY25 to Rs 41.6 crore in FY26 on project completion and inventory conversion.
- Medium-term adjacency opportunity from MLFF tolling, the wayside amenities programme, and ropeway development under Parvatmala Pariyojana; in EPC, the Madhya Pradesh pipeline and expanding opportunities in Gujarat and Goa support continued growth.
- The medium-term sector outlook remains positive, supported by continued public investment, road traffic growth and a sustained pipeline of highway and urban infrastructure development.
- Consolidated order book stood at Rs 1,133 crore as on March 31, 2026, comprising Rs 542 crore from tollway collection and Rs 591 crore from EPC Infrastructure, providing strong revenue visibility.
- The order book grew fivefold from Rs 225 crore in March 2023 to Rs 1,133 crore in March 2026, crossing the Rs 1,000 crore mark for the first time and closing 13% ahead of the internal target.
- EPC Infrastructure order book rose 42% from Rs 417 crore in March 2025 to Rs 591 crore in March 2026; the tollway collection order book grew 4.75x (375%) from Rs 114 crore to Rs 542 crore over the same period.
- The order book is predominantly composed of government projects, offering better execution certainty and enhanced payment security; government entities accounted for 64.9% of the EPC order book.
- From the current EPC order book, projects worth Rs 400-450 crore are targeted to be completed over the next two years.
- The active EPC bid pipeline is estimated at Rs 300-400 crore, with a historical win rate of 20-25%.
- HIL has completed 72 EPC projects with a cumulative value of Rs 712.5 crore and had 25 ongoing projects with balance work-in-hand of Rs 591.3 crore as of March 2026; as of March 31, 2026 it had completed 34 tollway projects and continues to operate 10 ongoing projects.
- In tollway collection, HIL had seven active contracts as of March 2026 with total contract value of Rs 765.8 crore and balance revenue of Rs 526.1 crore.
- A strong bid pipeline is being maintained with multiple tenders expected to open over the next six months.

Site-level safety protocols, trained safety personnel and mandatory incident reporting are in place, but the report states that 'further formalization through digital tracking and third party audits remains a stated priority' as the Company grows - i.e. safety assurance has not yet caught up with the scale of operations.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Highway Infrastructure Limited is an infrastructure development and management company with diversified operations across tollway collection, EPC infrastructure and real estate, operating across 11 states and one Union Territory.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: HIL operates and manages toll collection systems on highway stretches won through competitive bidding, principally under short-tenure Operate-Maintain-Transfer contracts with NHAI or the relevant government authority, where it pays a fixed weekly/daily sum irrespective of actual collections. It also executes EPC civil works spanning roads, bridges, irrigation works, tanks and civil buildings for public and private clients, including projects under PMAY, PMGSY and the Jal Jeevan Mission, and develops and sells residential and commercial property while earning lease rental income from hospitality and commercial assets. Tollway collection is the largest revenue driver, followed by EPC Infrastructure, with real estate the smallest vertical; activity is anchored in Madhya Pradesh with expanding presence in Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Chhattisgarh.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body: - Highway & Tondon Tollways Private Limited — subsidiary: The only subsidiary listed in Form AOC-1 Part A; acquired/subsidiary since 23rd April 2019; 51.00% shareholding. No associates or joint ventures are reported - Form AOC-1 Part B records 'NA' throughout.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Tollway Collection:** Operate-Maintain-Transfer (OMT) toll plaza operation and management, ANPR-based toll collection, Proprietary in-house toll management platform for real-time revenue monitoring and leakage control, Kaza Fee Plaza, Andhra Pradesh
- **EPC Infrastructure:** Roads, Bridges, Irrigation works and tanks, Civil buildings, Affordable housing (PMAY), Industrial areas, IT parks and schools
- **Real Estate:** Karuna Sagar residential project (822 flats), New York City gated residential colony, Commercial and hospitality property leasing

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Government agencies including NHAI, MPIDC, PWD, IDA, MPRRDA, MPBDC and AICTSL
- Operations across 11 states and 1 Union Territory in India
- Madhya Pradesh as the core EPC market, with expanding activity in Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat and Chhattisgarh
- Government schemes: PMAY, PMGSY and the Jal Jeevan Mission
- Private developers including the Kalyan Group, Shubham Group and ISBI Developers
- Residential and commercial real estate buyers and lessees in Madhya Pradesh

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Government infrastructure-led development remains the primary demand driver, with infrastructure capital outlay projected to reach Rs 13.1 lakh crore by FY27, roughly 14% above FY26, and continued support from the National Infrastructure Pipeline, PM Gati Shakti and the National Monetisation Pipeline.
- Higher allocation to road and highway development, continued expressway execution and rising toll collections create a favourable backdrop for both of HIL's main operating segments.
- Toll collection demand is underpinned by an expanding national highway network, PPP participation, economic and trade growth lifting freight traffic, urbanisation, and electronic tolling technology (ETC, RFID, real-time traffic management) that improves collection efficiency.
- Near-universal FASTag penetration improves toll realisation and minimises revenue leakage, supporting predictable and transparent cash flows for toll operators.
- The Indore and wider Madhya Pradesh operating environment is supportive: the Indore Municipal Corporation's sanctioned budget focused on road construction, upgradation, maintenance and restoration works gives regionally established EPC contractors execution visibility.
- Under the OMT model, fixed weekly/daily payments to NHAI are independent of actual toll collected, so revenue upside above the bid assumption accrues to the operator while short tenure allows faster capital turnover and limits long-term asset risk.
- Better enforcement, lane discipline and FASTag penetration are the stated margin levers in toll operations; in EPC, margin is protected by the 13-14% gross profit bidding floor.
- Mix shift: Tollway Collection contributed 73.7% of FY26 consolidated revenue, EPC Infrastructure 19.8% and Real Estate & Others 6.5%, with Real Estate revenue stepping up from Rs 8.0 crore in FY25 to Rs 41.6 crore in FY26 on project completion and inventory conversion.
- Medium-term adjacency opportunity from MLFF tolling, the wayside amenities programme, and ropeway development under Parvatmala Pariyojana; in EPC, the Madhya Pradesh pipeline and expanding opportunities in Gujarat and Goa support continued growth.
- The medium-term sector outlook remains positive, supported by continued public investment, road traffic growth and a sustained pipeline of highway and urban infrastructure development.
- Consolidated order book stood at Rs 1,133 crore as on March 31, 2026, comprising Rs 542 crore from tollway collection and Rs 591 crore from EPC Infrastructure, providing strong revenue visibility.
- The order book grew fivefold from Rs 225 crore in March 2023 to Rs 1,133 crore in March 2026, crossing the Rs 1,000 crore mark for the first time and closing 13% ahead of the internal target.
- EPC Infrastructure order book rose 42% from Rs 417 crore in March 2025 to Rs 591 crore in March 2026; the tollway collection order book grew 4.75x (375%) from Rs 114 crore to Rs 542 crore over the same period.
- The order book is predominantly composed of government projects, offering better execution certainty and enhanced payment security; government entities accounted for 64.9% of the EPC order book.
- From the current EPC order book, projects worth Rs 400-450 crore are targeted to be completed over the next two years.
- The active EPC bid pipeline is estimated at Rs 300-400 crore, with a historical win rate of 20-25%.
- HIL has completed 72 EPC projects with a cumulative value of Rs 712.5 crore and had 25 ongoing projects with balance work-in-hand of Rs 591.3 crore as of March 2026; as of March 31, 2026 it had completed 34 tollway projects and continues to operate 10 ongoing projects.
- In tollway collection, HIL had seven active contracts as of March 2026 with total contract value of Rs 765.8 crore and balance revenue of Rs 526.1 crore.
- A strong bid pipeline is being maintained with multiple tenders expected to open over the next six months.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Four-pillar growth strategy: growth through scale and adjacency, operational excellence, geographic expansion, and disciplined balance sheet management.
- Scale the core verticals through selective, margin-disciplined bidding, holding a stated gross profit discipline of 13-14% and a willingness to exit non-viable contracts rather than chase low-quality volume.
- Expand from the central India base into Gujarat, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and the Northeast, with a longer-term aim of broadening presence further across India to diversify revenue concentration and deepen access to new order flows.
- Measured entry into adjacencies aligned with existing mobility-infrastructure credentials: wayside amenities and ancillary services alongside toll corridors (food courts, fuel stations, EV charging, warehousing, driver facilities), renewable energy including solar EPC and EV charging infrastructure, and potential participation in ropeways and HAM projects under Parvatmala Pariyojana.
- Prioritise traffic-intensive corridors to maximise toll collection revenue, and undertake larger EPC projects either independently or through joint ventures.
- Leverage the proprietary in-house toll monitoring and site-management technology (including ANPR experience) as the operating edge in Tollway Collection and to create synergies across infrastructure segments.
- Monetise real estate faster through residential delivery plus commercial and hospitality leasing for recurring income.
- Maintain balance sheet quality, leverage discipline and returns as the Company scales; debt to equity was reduced from 0.9x to 0.45x over FY23-FY26 and net worth increased to Rs 228.5 crore.
- Long-term intent to build a larger, more diversified mobility infrastructure platform with broader geographic presence and stronger recurring income streams.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: HIL's expansion in this bundle is described as footprint and adjacency build-out rather than plant capex. Geographically, the Company is expanding from its central India base into Gujarat, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh and the Northeast, with a longer-term target to broaden its presence further across India in order to diversify revenue concentration and deepen access to new order flows. Growth through scale and adjacency is a stated pillar, with four adjacencies under evaluation: commercial leasing and real estate monetisation through hospitality and commercial properties; ancillary services alongside toll corridors including food courts, fuel stations, EV charging, warehousing and driver facilities; potential participation in ropeways and HAM projects under Parvatmala Pariyojana; and renewable energy opportunities including solar EPC and EV charging infrastructure. The Company has already commissioned EV charging infrastructure under the AICTSL contract in Indore and is evaluating renewable energy EPC as a growth area. Over the medium term, MLFF tolling, the wayside amenities programme and ropeway development under Parvatmala Pariyojana are identified as meaningful adjacency opportunities, while in EPC the project pipeline in Madhya Pradesh and expanding opportunities in Gujarat and Goa support continued growth. Funding capacity was strengthened during FY26: the Company listed on the BSE and NSE on 12 August 2025 and raised Rs 130 crore through the IPO, which the report says strengthened the capital base to support future expansion and strategic initiatives; net worth rose to Rs 228.5 crore and debt to equity improved from 0.9x to 0.45x over FY23-FY26. No rupee capital-expenditure quantum, project cost, commissioning date or capacity addition is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Three decades of execution experience across multiple infrastructure asset classes, with more than 100 projects completed since 1995
- Established, long-standing relationships with government agencies including NHAI, MPIDC, PWD, IDA and MPRRDA
- Proprietary toll management platform developed in-house for real-time revenue monitoring, discrepancy detection, leakage control and site-level management, giving stronger operational control and a more efficient cost structure
- Among the select toll operators to have implemented ANPR-based toll collection, with toll plazas operated on major inter-state and intra-state expressways
- Asset-light OMT toll model: short contract tenure recycles working capital quickly and carries no long-term exposure to asset degradation or major rehabilitation costs
- Capital discipline: a stated gross profit floor of 13-14% in bidding rather than pursuing low-quality volume
- Government entities account for 64.9% of the EPC order book, offering execution certainty and payment security

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Government policy and budgetary dependence — The forward-looking statement explicitly names changes in government policy and economic conditions as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. The demand narrative in this bundle rests almost entirely on public spending - Union Budget capital outlay, MoRTH and NHAI allocations, NIP, PM Gati Shakti and the National Monetisation Pipeline - so a slowdown in state capex or a change in tolling/highway policy directly compresses both order inflow and toll opportunity.
- Project execution risk — Project execution is named in the forward-looking statement as a risk factor. The Company's stated long-term positioning - 'the future will be shaped by execution, contract by contract' - and its record order book mean value is realised only on delivery; slippage on active contracts converts a record book into deferred revenue.
- Competitive intensity in bidding — Competition is listed as a risk factor in the forward-looking statement, and growth is explicitly framed as depending on 'selective, margin disciplined bidding'. Aggressive bidding by peers either costs the Company work or forces it below its stated margin thresholds.
- Segment and revenue concentration — Tollway Collection accounted for 73.7% of FY26 consolidated revenue, with EPC Infrastructure 19.8% and Real Estate and Others 6.5%. Management's own rationale for geographic expansion is that it 'is intended to diversify revenue concentration', which acknowledges that current revenue is concentrated by both segment and geography (a central India base).
- Growth dependent on entry into unproven adjacencies — A stated pillar of growth is measured entry into wayside amenities, renewable energy EPC, ropeways and HAM projects under Parvatmala Pariyojana, plus MLFF tolling - all described as opportunities under evaluation rather than businesses with an operating track record, so the growth case carries execution and learning-curve risk in segments new to the Company.
- Balance sheet leverage as the Company scales — The Company treats leverage as an active watch item: debt to equity was reduced from 0.9x to 0.45x over FY23-FY26 and management 'remains focused on balance sheet quality, leverage discipline, and returns' as it scales - implying that funding a fivefold order book without re-levering is a live constraint.
- Environmental and clearance compliance at construction sites — Environmental priorities are stated as responsible material usage, dust and noise management at construction sites, and compliance with clearance conditions - a structural exposure for a civil-construction contractor, where a clearance breach can halt a site.
- Safety framework still being formalised — Site-level safety protocols, trained safety personnel and mandatory incident reporting are in place, but the report states that 'further formalization through digital tracking and third party audits remains a stated priority' as the Company grows - i.e. safety assurance has not yet caught up with the scale of operations.
